description: Fetching, sending, and handling real data over HTTP: fetch/JSON, REST conventions, error handling, loading states, and authentication basics.

lessons.title: What Is an API?
lessons.description: Understand APIs as defined contracts between software systems, and learn to read an API's endpoints, parameters, request/response shapes, and documented behavior instead of treating 'the API' as a mysterious black box.
lessons.originalIntent: Understand APIs as defined contracts between software systems, and learn to read an API's endpoints, parameters, request/response shapes, and documented behavior instead of treating 'the API' as a mysterious black box.

lessons.title: HTTP Requests and Responses
lessons.description: Understand the structure of HTTP requests and responses, including methods, paths, headers, bodies, and status codes, so you can reason about network communication before using Fetch.
lessons.originalIntent: Understand the structure of HTTP requests and responses, including methods, paths, headers, bodies, and status codes, so you can reason about network communication before using Fetch.

lessons.title: JSON
lessons.description: Understand JSON as a text format for structured data exchange and practice converting between JSON text and JavaScript values with JSON.parse and JSON.stringify.
lessons.originalIntent: Understand JSON as a text format for structured data exchange and practice converting between JSON text and JavaScript values with JSON.parse and JSON.stringify.

lessons.title: HTTP Status Codes
lessons.description: Learn to read HTTP status codes as meaningful signals about the outcome of a request, with emphasis on the 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, and 5xx response classes.
lessons.originalIntent: Learn to read HTTP status codes as meaningful signals about the outcome of a request, with emphasis on the 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, and 5xx response classes.

lessons.title: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE
lessons.description: Understand the intended semantics of the main HTTP methods and practice choosing the appropriate method for reading, creating, replacing, partially updating, and deleting resources.
lessons.originalIntent: Understand the intended semantics of the main HTTP methods and practice choosing the appropriate method for reading, creating, replacing, partially updating, and deleting resources.

lessons.title: Loading, Error, and Empty States
lessons.description: Design and implement explicit loading, error, and empty states so data-driven interfaces remain understandable when data is delayed, unavailable, or simply absent.
lessons.originalIntent: Design and implement explicit loading, error, and empty states so data-driven interfaces remain understandable when data is delayed, unavailable, or simply absent.

lessons.title: Working with Fetch
lessons.description: Use fetch() to make HTTP requests from JavaScript, inspect the response, handle JSON data, and deliberately handle HTTP failures instead of assuming a rejected Promise means every failed HTTP status.
lessons.originalIntent: Use fetch() to make HTTP requests from JavaScript, inspect the response, handle JSON data, and deliberately handle HTTP failures instead of assuming a rejected Promise means every failed HTTP status.

lessons.title: API Integration Project
lessons.description: Build a working frontend feature that consumes a real API and handles loading, success, empty, and error states without hardcoding an ideal response shape.
lessons.originalIntent: Build a working frontend feature that consumes a real API and handles loading, success, empty, and error states without hardcoding an ideal response shape.
